newsitem.title: INDIA: Sixteen killed after truck hits India power line.
newsitem.headline: Sixteen killed after truck hits India power line.

text.p: Sixteen people were killed when a truck carrying Shia Moslems observing the mourning month of Muharram hit an overhead power line, caught fire and crashed, police said on Tuesday.
They said the truck was carrying about 50 people and three "tazias," or holy replicas of tombs made of cane, paper and wire, which hit the power transmission wire.
Eleven people were seriously burned in the accident late on Monday in the western town of Dag. Dag is some 450 km (270 miles) southeast of Jaipur, the capital of the northwestern state of Rajasthan.
Shia Moslems mourn the slaying of Hussain, grandson of the Prophet Mohammad during the first Islamic month of Muharram.
According to local tradition, the "tazias" are immersed in a nearby river after a mourning procession to mark the martyrdom of Hussain.
Police said the truck had been carrying the "tazias" to a local dam.
